emergencyNumber: 116 (police), 118 (fire), no reliable national ambulance number — go directly to hospital or clinic
healthcareSystem: Basic public healthcare system supplemented by private clinics and NGO-run facilities. Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital (EFSTH) in Banjul is the main referral hospital. Private clinics in the tourist coastal area offer better care. The system is severely underfunded.
qualityNotes: Private clinics in the Senegambia tourist area and Banjul offer reasonable basic care. EFSTH handles more complex cases but is under-resourced. NGO-supported clinics provide good primary care. For serious conditions, evacuation to Dakar (Senegal) or Europe is necessary. Quality drops significantly upcountry.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in the coastal tourist area and Banjul open 8am-7pm. Some pharmacies in tourist areas have extended hours. Limited pharmacy access upcountry.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in the tourist coastal strip (Kololi, Senegambia, Kotu) are reasonably stocked with common medications. Staff speak English. Counterfeit drugs exist — buy only from licensed pharmacies. Bring essential and specialized medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement varies. Many medications available without strict prescription. Focus on buying from licensed pharmacies to ensure quality and authenticity.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal. Drug laws are strict with severe penalties including imprisonment.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. Carry a doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry documentation from your prescribing physician.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. English documentation is accepted. Bring your full supply as specific medications may not be available or may be counterfeit.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is essential. Serious conditions require evacuation to Dakar, Senegal or Europe. Ensure malaria treatment is covered. The Gambia is a popular budget destination — do not skimp on travel insurance.

recommended: Meningococcal meningitis (especially during dry season December-June)
Malaria prophylaxis (essential — malaria is endemic throughout The Gambia)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever vaccination certificate is REQUIRED for entry. Malaria is a serious risk year-round, with highest transmission during and after the rainy season (June-November). Prophylaxis is essential.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink. Use sealed bottled water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside of international hotels. Bottled water is widely available in the tourist coastal area. Carry purification tablets for upcountry travel.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants in the tourist areas. Fresh fish and grilled meats from busy beach restaurants are generally safe when cooked thoroughly. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruit. Benachin (jollof rice) and domoda (groundnut stew) are popular and usually safe when freshly prepared and hot.
medicalTourismNote: The Gambia is not a medical tourism destination. For advanced care, patients travel to Senegal, Morocco, or Europe.
metaDescription: Gambia health guide for travelers. Emergency contacts, yellow fever vaccine required, malaria prevention, unsafe water advisory, and pharmacy information.

hospitals.name: Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital (EFSTH)
hospitals.notes: Main government referral hospital. English-speaking staff. Overcrowded and under-equipped but handles emergencies. Located in the capital.

hospitals.name: Medical Research Council (MRC) Unit
hospitals.notes: Well-equipped research facility that provides some clinical services. Excellent for tropical disease diagnosis. Near the tourist area.

hospitals.name: Afri Med Clinic
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in the main tourist area. Popular with tourists and expats. General consultations and minor treatments.

dentalCare.availability: Limited. A few dental clinics in the Banjul/tourist coastal area. None upcountry.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic. Some private dentists in the tourist area can handle routine treatments. Complex dental work requires travel abroad.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, private clinics in the Senegambia area can do extractions. Pack a dental emergency kit for upcountry travel.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very few. Some NGOs provide counseling services.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Tanka Tanka Psychiatric Hospital near Banjul is the main mental health facility. Stigma around mental illness remains significant. Some NGO-supported counseling is available.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited. Tourist hotels may have some accessible rooms but public spaces lack accessibility features. Sandy beaches and unpaved roads present challenges.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals have basic entry access but are not designed for wheelchair users.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Tourist taxis can be arranged. Some resorts offer assistance.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact your hotel in advance about accessibility. The tourist coastal area is relatively flat. Beach wheelchairs are not commonly available. Hiring a local guide is helpful.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at EFSTH and some private clinics.
covidStatus.notes: COVID situation has stabilized. Healthcare capacity remains limited.

insuranceClaimProcess: Keep all receipts and medical documentation. Most facilities require cash payment upfront. Gambian dalasi (GMD) is the local currency. Submit claims with receipts to your insurer after returning home. Contact your insurer's emergency line before seeking treatment if possible.

commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs are low but quality varies significantly. Private clinics in the tourist area charge more but provide better care. Cash payment is standard.

medicalEvacuation.note: Dakar is the primary evacuation destination — less than an hour by air. Banjul International Airport is the departure point. For serious injuries or cardiac events, evacuation is essential. Many UK tour operators include evacuation coordination.

drugNameMap.note: Widely available at licensed pharmacies. Check expiry dates.
